sources.title: PIA19658 Titan global map, June 2015: Cassini ISS 938 nm (NASA/JPL-Caltech/Space Science Institute)
USGS Titan Cassini ISS Global Mosaic 4005m
PIA20016 Peering through Titan's haze: Cassini VIMS infrared views
IAU Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature: Titan

assets.credit: Reference: NASA/JPL-Caltech/Space Science Institute, University of Arizona (Cassini ISS, VIMS, RADAR); IAU/USGS nomenclature. Procedural reconstruction of the near-infrared ground, with a haze limb added in the game
assets.projection: 2:1 equirectangular; north up, east-positive, 0° E at the centre (IAU_TITAN). Named features at their IAU centres; region outlines traced by eye, so edges are approximate.
assets.notes: Titan's ground as Cassini saw it through the haze in the near infrared, not its visible-light (haze) appearance: dark equatorial dune seas (Shangri-La, Belet, Senkyo, Fensal, Aztlan) around bright Xanadu, Adiri, Dilmun, Quivira and Tsegihi; the seas Kraken, Ligeia and Punga and a lake district in the north, Ontario Lacus in the south; craters Menrva, Sinlap, Selk, Afekan, Soi, Forseti, Hano, Ksa and Guabonito. Dune streaks are drawn coarser than the real ~3 km spacing. The game adds a haze limb in its shader (MOON_SURFACES.Titan.haze). Replaces the earlier unregistered NASA 3D Resources concept texture.
assets.processing: 2048x1024 greyscale PNG, JPEG quality 82 via sips.
